profiles.meeting_scenario: At a trademark litigation firm, the team is conducting a design review of a draft expert declaration from a historical linguist for a summary-judgment filing in MealWise Labs v. Nutriwise, a Lanham Act dispute over how much protection the plaintiff can claim in marks built around the element "-wise." The declaration argues that English "wise" underwent grammaticalization from an independent noun into a productive suffix, which supports the defense position that the element is weak and widely available. The specific draft section under review quotes secondary literature discussing Condillac and Horne Tooke as early observers of grammaticalization. The agenda is to decide whether the declaration structure, source support, and appendix design are sufficient for the upcoming filing. The expected outcome is a go/no-go decision on the draft and a short list of revisions before it goes either to the expert or directly into filing prep.

members.name: Nora Feld
members.expertise: Trademark briefing, expert declaration drafting, evidentiary support for summary judgment
members.background: Nora manages the day-to-day briefing in federal Lanham Act cases and previously clerked for a district judge; she often translates subject-matter experts' academic material into litigation-ready declarations.
members.private_state: She wants the expert declaration approved quickly so she can keep the summary-judgment schedule on track, and she is trying to avoid reopening the expert's prose structure because the expert is slow to turn revisions.
hidden_assumptions: "Historical sources" in this declaration means canonical linguistic authorities that establish the concept's pedigree, regardless of whether the source predates the plaintiff's first use date.
A declaration is "ready" once the substantive theory and quoted passages are stable; exhibit assembly, translations, and formal evidentiary packaging can happen during filing prep.
The design review covers the declaration text and exhibit list, not the downstream mechanics of certified translations or source authentication.
When the team says "the Tooke cite," it refers to the 1786 volume excerpted in her research memo unless someone specifies otherwise.

members.name: Daniel Ibarra
members.expertise: Trademark distinctiveness disputes, dispositive-motion strategy, appellate framing of expert evidence
members.background: Daniel leads briefing strategy in IP cases and is known for scrutinizing whether expert material will survive record-based challenges rather than just read persuasively on paper.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid any evidentiary weakness that could let the other side attack the declaration as academic but unusable, and he is mentally reviewing the draft as if it were already attached to next week's motion papers.
hidden_assumptions: "Historical" support in this case means evidence that clearly predates MealWise's claimed first commercial use in 2009, because timing is what makes the point legally valuable.
If a draft is described as "ready for filing," it should already be attachable to the motion without needing foundational repairs or additional appendices.
Because the declaration leans on French and eighteenth-century sources, the appendix should already contain courtroom-usable translations and enough information to authenticate the excerpts.
When someone says "Tooke," that ordinarily means the combined Diversions of Purley work, including the later 1805 volume where the prepositions point is developed.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss whether the declaration has enough "historical support" for grammaticalization.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the draft should cite respected early thinkers and modern scholarship showing the idea is longstanding in linguistics.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the support should include materials that clearly predate the plaintiff's 2009 first-use claim, because that is the legally useful historical window.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a trademark case about linguistic history, "historical support" sounds naturally sufficient to both of them; each hears a familiar phrase from their own workflow and sees no reason to unpack the time frame.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both use the language of whether the declaration is "ready" or can be "filed next week."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes "ready" means substantively complete enough to send to the expert for final sign-off, with technical cleanup still to come.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes "ready for filing" means the exhibit package, translations, and evidentiary vulnerabilities have already been resolved.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Lawyers routinely use "ready" as shorthand at multiple stages of drafting, and both expect some polishing, so the difference in threshold remains hidden behind ordinary project language.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to tightening or finalizing "the appendix" to support the declaration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the appendix means the set of quoted source excerpts and bibliography attached to the expert declaration, with translation certification and source-authentication materials handled separately later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the appendix includes everything the court would need to use those sources immediately, including certified translations of the Condillac excerpt and foundation for the scans.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Appendix-building is often split across associates, paralegals, and filing teams, so each person casually collapses different pieces of that workflow into the same label without noticing.

misalignment_points.topic: Which Tooke source is being referenced
misalignment_points.surface_form: They mention relying on "the Tooke section" or "the Tooke cite" for the prepositions point.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the 1786 volume already excerpted in her draft materials.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the 1805 volume, where he recalls the derivation-of-prepositions discussion being more directly useful.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both volumes are commonly cited together under the same work title and author, and internal shorthand treats them as one source family, so the specific volume never gets named.
